fixes.change: operator new/new[] get __attribute__((section("__lcxx_override"))); operator delete delegates to free(ptr) with the RAW pointer (HobbyOS free_locked BLOCK_MAGIC check distinguishes stashed vs raw payloads)
fixes.rationale: w5-nothrow os_wide_followup: any OS userland program linking cxxrt.o + -fno-exceptions libc++ that calls new(nothrow) (raw malloc payload) then delete had the latent free(BLOCK_MAGIC) data abort; and the throwing new's section address vs libc++'s nothrow-override check
fixes.verification: cxxrt_test_host: 25 checks 0 failures (link now includes obj/host_malloc_hb.o + strong hb_* wrappers in the test TU — the free(ptr) contract is defined over the HobbyOS allocator, glibc free() corrupts on the aligned stash); llvm-nm: _Znwm/_Znam inside __lcxx_override, host + aarch64 obj
fixes.note: host test now backed by the real allocator instead of glibc — the alignment/new-delete assertions test the actual on-device semantics

fixes.symptom: S1's first in-OS link failed: 'lld is a generic driver. Invoke ld.lld (Unix)..'
fixes.root_cause: lld v21 is the unified driver; invoked as bare lld (our frozen F1 name LLD.BIN) it requires a driver-mode flag because argv[0] is not ld.lld.  The host Makefile uses the ld.lld symlink and never sees this.
fixes.verification: host: bare lld fails identically, -flavor gnu links the same ARM ELF set; in-OS S1 all 4 links passed

fixes.change: proc_marshal_argv per-arg temp 64 -> 1024; sys_exec flat-args argbuf 256 -> 1024 and per-arg 64 -> 1024 (both arches)
fixes.symptom: S0 blocked at `CLANG: error: no input files` even though the identical command line compiles when run directly in-OS
fixes.root_cause: make runs recipe lines as `sh -c '<line>'` — the whole 200+ char line is ONE argv element; the execv marshal capped each element at 63 chars, truncating the line mid-token; sh then tokenized a partial command (argc 16 -> 7 via argvprobe) and clang saw no input TU
fixes.verification: post-fix S0: phase=s0-check-done rc=0 + ACCEPTANCE-COMPLETE; check.o (21144 B) pulled off the image, valid AArch64 ELF REL; x64 trap.o host compile-checked

walls_and_handoffs.what: in-OS clang under ARM TCG is ~900-1500x slower than the host (measured). The whole 59-TU kernel host-compiles in 5.8 s, so S2 projects to ~90-150 min TCG; S3's in-OS disk assembly and S1's links carry the same multiplier
walls_and_handoffs.recommendation: run S2 (and S3) as a long single boot with a >= 3h QEMU budget, or split per-TU, or run the acceptance on faster hardware/KVM (x64 selfhost path would need an x64 toolchain build — out of acceptance scope). If the lane must not run hours: capture per-TU progress via phase=kernel-compile rc=0 markers and hand off the count
